title: Population distribution in Eastern Africa
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use a density map of the region and country areas and populations (teacher to give current figures). Density = people ÷ area.

skills.key_step: The child explains what makes places crowded (rain, soil, water, jobs, peace) or empty (dry, steep, forest, insecurity).

floor.prerequisite: Says where density is high and low in Kenya.
floor.question: Is the Lake Victoria basin densely or sparsely populated?

representations: a density map and a rainfall map side by side
steps: Check its rain, soil and jobs.

board.do: Draw two areas: one with rain clouds and farms, one with sand.

board.say: Why do few people live here?

misconceptions.ask: Why do few people live in a desert?
misconceptions.repair: Ask where a family would find water and food.

misconceptions.ask: Which place is more likely to be crowded?
misconceptions.repair: Ask where it is easier to build and grow crops.

listen_for: They do not; towns push people away
misconceptions.ask: Why do many people move to Nairobi and Kampala?
misconceptions.repair: List what a town offers that a village may not.

misconceptions.ask: Are thick rain forests densely populated?
misconceptions.repair: Compare the density map with the forest map.

checks.question: Give two factors that attract many people to an area.
checks.answer: any two of: reliable rain, fertile soil, water, jobs, roads, peace

checks.question: Why do few people live in the Chalbi Desert?
checks.answer: it is very dry with little water

skills.key_step: The child locates crowded and empty areas of the region and keeps density apart from total population.

floor.question: Give one reason people crowd near Lake Victoria.

representations: a table of people and area

board.do: Write: Country A 10 million people, 25,000 square km; Country B 100 million people, 1,000,000 square km.

board.say: Which has more people per square km?

board.do: Write A: 400 per square km, B: 100 per square km.

misconceptions.ask: Density is the number of people for what?
misconceptions.repair: Compare two countries by people per square kilometre in a small table.

misconceptions.ask: Which country has high population density?
misconceptions.repair: Give people and area for a small and a large country and divide.

misconceptions.ask: Ethiopia is much bigger than Rwanda. Which has the higher density?
misconceptions.repair: Divide people by area for both, with rounded figures.

misconceptions.ask: Nairobi is crowded. Is all of Kenya densely populated?
misconceptions.repair: Shade Kenya on a density map: dark in some places, light in others.

checks.question: Name an area of high population density in Eastern Africa.
checks.answer: any of: the Lake Victoria basin, Kenya highlands, Ethiopian highlands, Rwanda, Burundi, a big city

checks.question: Does the country with the most people always have the highest density?
checks.answer: No, density depends on area too

skills.key_step: The child gives the effects of high population density.
representations: a drawing of a growing town
steps: Ask what happens to land, jobs and services.
Suggest a way to manage it.

board.do: Draw a field split into four, then into sixteen.

board.say: What has happened to each family's farm?

board.do: Write land shortage and two more effects.

misconceptions.ask: What happens to farms when families grow large in a crowded area?
misconceptions.repair: Cut a paper farm among more and more children.

listen_for: They have too few learners and patients
misconceptions.ask: What pressure does a crowded area put on schools and hospitals?
misconceptions.repair: Count seats in a class of 90.

misconceptions.ask: Why do slums grow in crowded cities?
misconceptions.repair: Count houses and families on a drawing of a growing town.

misconceptions.ask: How can high population density harm forests?
misconceptions.repair: Show a before-and-after photo of a cleared hill.

checks.question: Give two effects of high population density.
checks.answer: any two of: land shortage, food shortage, unemployment, pressure on services, forest clearing, slums, pollution

checks.question: Why are classrooms crowded where density is high?
checks.answer: many children and not enough schools
